body:
## Environment

- uv 0.12.15 (`uv-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`)
- OS: Linux (x86_64), CPython 3.12

## Steps to reproduce

Public repo [paperless-ngx/paperless-ngx](https://github.com/paperless-ngx/paperless-ngx) at `5f17b1a310aa011f43b56474221d97f8d6bfe689`. The project requires `torch>=2.13,<2.15` from a `pytorch-cpu` index, and its `uv.lock` uses forked resolution and has Git sources.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/paperless-ngx/paperless-ngx && cd paperless-ngx
git checkout 5f17b1a310aa011f43b56474221d97f8d6bfe689

# One --upgrade-package flag for every non-Git package in uv.lock
ARGS=$(python3 - <<'PY'
import tomllib
lock = tomllib.load(open("uv.lock", "rb"))
names = sorted({p["name"] for p in lock["package"] if "git" not in p.get("source", {})})
print(" ".join(f"--upgrade-package {n}" for n in names))
PY
)

uv lock --python 3.12 $ARGS   # pass 1: exit 0 (torch 2.14.0 -> 2.14.1)
uv lock --python 3.12 --locked   # exit 0: the new lock is up to date
uv lock --python 3.12 $ARGS   # pass 2: exit 1
```

## Expected

Pass 2 succeeds, since `uv lock --locked` accepts the lock that pass 1 wrote, and makes no further change or only a small one.

## Actual

```text
error: No solution found when resolving dependencies for split (markers: python_full_version >= '3.15' and platform_python_implementation == 'PyPy' and sys_platform == 'darwin')
  cause: Because torch>=2.13.0 has no macOS-compatible wheels and your project depends on torch>=2.13, we can conclude that your project's requirements are unsatisfiable.
         And because your project requires paperless-ngx[mariadb], we can conclude that your project's requirements are unsatisfiable.
```

`uv lock --upgrade` (with no package names) succeeds on both passes, and so does a plain `uv lock` on the pass 1 lock. Only the `--upgrade-package` form fails, and only when run on its own output. The first pass adds forks to `resolution-markers`, including `python_full_version >= '3.15' and platform_python_implementation == 'PyPy' and sys_platform == 'darwin'`. Re-solving that fork with every package marked for upgrade appears to lose the fallback that the first pass found.

## Context

We drive `uv lock --upgrade-package` for every registry package (rather than `--upgrade`) so that Git-pinned sources stay where they are, then run it a second time because the first run can leave `resolution-markers` in an order a second run changes (see #22040).

---
Found by an automated test of a dependency-update tool across public repositories.
title: `uv lock --upgrade-package` fails with "No solution found" on a lock the same command just wrote
